subject: Post-call: SDK lab handoff and local test artifacts
messages:
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Sana Patel <sana@brightpathhealth.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 29 Nov 2026 14:12:00 -0800
Subject: Post-call: SDK lab handoff and local test artifacts

Hi Sana — thanks again for taking the call this morning. Quick recap and concrete next steps for the SDK lab we discussed with your platform team: 

1) Goal: get your engineers running a local end-to-end sample that mirrors the production inference path (auth, routing to a fallback model, embeddings for semantic search, and a small reranker).

2) We attached a test bundle (redwood-sdklab-scripts-v1.zip) with two sample apps (python_api_demo, ts_chat_worker), a local-test-checklist.md, and an auth-routing-mapping.csv that shows route names we recommend for dev vs. prod.

3) Immediate asks for BrightPath: please confirm which internal git host we should push the sample app to (if any), and whether your CI runners have Docker-in-Docker enabled — that affects our local container approach.

Proposed next steps (we can do these this week):
- Karthik to run a 60-minute pairing session with one of your infra engineers (pair debugging the auth flow and routing policy).
- Marissa to share a trimmed-down test dataset and a suggested evaluation prompt set for reranker tuning.
- Sana to confirm availability and preferred engineer for the pairing (ideally someone with access to the staging KMS).

Attachments: redwood-sdklab-scripts-v1.zip (bundle, includes code and README), local-test-checklist.md (step-by-step), auth-routing-mapping.csv (route names and sample policies).

If it helps, Karthik and I can run the first 30 minutes as an overview and use the remainder for the hands-on setup.

Thanks — Hannah
Hannah Schmitt
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
hannah.schmitt@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0123

From: Sana Patel <sana@brightpathhealth.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 29 Nov 2026 17:05:00 -05:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: SDK lab handoff and local test artifacts

Thanks Hannah — that all looks good. Quick answers:
- We use Bitbucket for our sample repos (brightpath/platform-sdks) — please push as a branch and we'll open an internal review.
- CI: our staging runners do not support Docker-in-Docker; we have a small Kubernetes sandbox (namespaces per team) where we can run sidecar containers.

Can Karthik pair with our infra lead, Miguel Alvarez (miguel.alvarez@brightpathhealth.com)? He has KMS access for staging. Miguel is available Tue 12–2pm PT or Wed 9–11am PT.

Also can you confirm the Python sample uses the same token-rotation pattern we discussed (short-lived tokens + refresh via internal auth service)? We need to validate that before we let it run against staging KMS.

Sana
Sana Patel
Head of Platform, BrightPath Health
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>

Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 08:22:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: SDK lab handoff and local test artifacts

Hi Miguel / Sana — looping in a short technical runbook and the local-test checklist so we have a concrete plan for the pairing session. See highlights below and notes in the attached checklist.

High-level plan for pairing (60 min):
- 00–10: confirm staging network access + KMS permissions.
- 10–25: walk through the python_api_demo (local mode): how to set REDWOOD_BASE_URL, token refresh flow, and run the embedded reranker test.
- 25–45: reproduce an auth-routing mismatch that we commonly see (incorrect route header) and apply the mapping in auth-routing-mapping.csv.
- 45–60: smoke test full flow (embed -> index -> query -> rerank) and capture logs for follow-up.

Local dev notes (from the bundle):
- python_api_demo uses short-lived token -> refresh endpoint pattern. The README describes a sample refresh server (refresh_server.py) that returns a rotated token and expiry. Please do NOT point refresh_server to production KMS; we will provide a staging key ARN to test against.
- TS sample (ts_chat_worker) demonstrates tool-calling structured output via a local function stub (tools/health_lookup.ts) and shows how to parse the structured JSON output into reranker candidates.
- We included a small embedded dataset (embeds_sample.jsonl, no PII) for the reranker smoke test.

Attachments referenced in the bundle: local-test-checklist.md (step-by-step smoke tests), auth-routing-mapping.csv (header->route mapping).

Miguel / Sana: are you OK scheduling Tue 2026-12-01 12:30–1:30pm PT? If that slot works, I'll send a calendar invite with the pairing repo and the Drive link.

Thanks — Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Principal Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
